contract.reader: An engineer or student who knows the feedback loop and the proportional offset (Foundations of Control Systems, entries 1 and 2) and has to commission or tune temperature, level, flow or pressure loops in a PLC or DCS
contract.problem: How to get a usable model of a process, what a real PID block does beyond the textbook law, how to choose its settings and why loops of different kinds behave differently
contract.outcome: Identify an FOPDT model from a step test; convert between PID forms and units; explain derivative kick, filtering, windup and bumpless transfer; compute Ziegler-Nichols and SIMC settings and explain why the robust one is usually preferred; diagnose a slow level oscillation and suspect stiction
contract.contribution: One worked process (a heated vessel) carried from step test to tuning, with a standard-library simulation comparing two tuning rules on the nominal and a perturbed process and showing windup in numbers; the integrating-loop damping result
contract.evidence: Derivations in the text; two Python programs with their real output; Astrom and Hagglund (2006), Seborg et al. (2016), Shinskey (1996), Skogestad (2003), Ziegler and Nichols (1942)
contract.limitations: PI and PID only; no frequency-domain tuning, model-predictive control or gain scheduling; step-test data generated from the model, as the page says
